title: GitHub makes Copilot Fusion multi-model orchestration generally available
dek: Coding requests can take single-model, cascade or critique paths instead of binding every task to one manually selected model.
evidence: GitHub product disclosure and reported Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index comparison
takeaway: Treat model selection as an orchestration policy. Compare successful task cost and quality by route, including judge calls, retries and reviewer overhead.

sections.title: Context

bullets.detail: A single selected model can be excessive for routine edits and insufficient for hard debugging. Manual switching does not scale across heterogeneous tasks.

paragraphs: Static model selection: A single selected model can be excessive for routine edits and insufficient for hard debugging. Manual switching does not scale across heterogeneous tasks.

sections.title: What's new

bullets.detail: Fusion chooses Single (one model), Cascade (efficient draft checked and escalated to a stronger fresh-start answer when needed), or Critique (a second model reviews a draft and requests revision).
Standard, High and Max select an orchestration budget and model mix rather than a fixed model. Enterprise policies constrain which models Fusion can select.
Fusion is generally available in VS Code, Copilot CLI, the Copilot app and JetBrains. Each underlying model is billed at its standard rate, with a temporary 30% Fusion discount on paid plans.

paragraphs: Three execution paths: Fusion chooses Single (one model), Cascade (efficient draft checked and escalated to a stronger fresh-start answer when needed), or Critique (a second model reviews a draft and requests revision).
Effort controls: Standard, High and Max select an orchestration budget and model mix rather than a fixed model. Enterprise policies constrain which models Fusion can select.

sections.title: Evidence & limitations

bullets.detail: GitHub reports Copilot Fusion Max scoring 60 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, within two points of Claude Code with Opus 5.5 Max. GitHub says the Fusion run used about half the API cost and tokens and took roughly 40% less time per task.
Those figures describe one evaluated coding-agent configuration. They do not establish the same savings for every repository, task distribution, model policy or human-review workflow.
A judge can accept an incorrect efficient-model draft, while a critique loop can add cost and latency without fixing the error. A task-average score hides these route-specific failures.
